text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- Bosnian Serb Republic President Biljana Plavsic disbands parliament, calls parliamentary elections for September 1. Bosnian Serb government declares her decision unconstitutional. Banja Luka TV stops broadcasts, claims journalists were under pressure to create a programme on Plavsic's dictate. Bosnian Serb TV broadcasting from studios in Pale and Bijeljina.

- Serbia's ruling Socialist party and parliamentary parties fail to reach agreement in second round of talks on election conditions. The Socialist and Radical parties in favour of raising the number of election units in Serbia to 29, most opposition parties opposed.
- Unless teachers are paid late wages, schools will not open their doors in September, warns Serbian Education Trade Union president Jagos Bulatovic.
- Fire in Pancevo oil refinery reason for petrol shortages. Serbian government says oil derivatives prices will not rise.

- Sale of hard currency in commercial banks achieved its goal -- dinar exchange rate stabilisation, central bank vice governor Zarko Trbojevic told a meeting of the Association of Yugoslav Banks. The number of banks must be reduced in an economically justifiable way, because the country does not need 100 financial organisations, said Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic.
- Belgium's Interbrew in talks with Niksic beer brewery on acquiring a 60 percent stake in the Montenegrin brewery for 25 million German marks.

- "I have nothing against another meeting with Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic," says Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic in interview to Belgrade weekly NIN. "Bosnia is open for Serbia but Serbia is not open for Bosnia," says Izetbegovic.
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and U.S. Envoy Robert Gelbard agree Bosnia's economic revival must be speeded up as a basis for overall normalisation of relations and life on territories where civil war was waged.

- Serbian government sets guaranteed price for 1997 wheat crop at 1.10 dinars per kilogram. Subsidised price of wheat protects producers interests, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic. Payments in three instalments by October.
- Yugoslavia, Macedonia sign agreement abolishing visas.
- Stability of the Bosnian Serb Republic is in Yugoslavia's interests, says ruling Socialist Party of Serbia spokesman Ivica Dacic.
BORBA

- Serbian Parliament speaker Dragan Tomic says law on privatisation will be on the agenda of the third extraordinary session of parliament, to be convened as soon as the second extraordinary session which is in progress now ends.
- The federal government to launch on July 10 second issue of treasury bills worth 200 million dinars at monthly interest rate of 3.5 percent to finance budget deficit.

- Administrative obstacles to free flow of goods, people and capital between Yugoslavia and Macedonia must be removed. Bilateral trade could reach $800 million in 1997, Yugoslav and Macedonian businessmen agree in talks.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) bodies are not informed officially of the content of requests for extraordinary party congress, said DPS deputy chairman Milica Pejanovic-Djurisic. They should be informed soon because some local party branches' requests for the congress to be held were made under pressure and threats, she said.

- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, on visit to Russia, meets with Patriarch Alexei II, Moscow Mayor Yuri Luskov and other officials and politicians, including Yegor Gaidar, leader of the Democratic Choice of Russia.

- Cooperation between offices of state prosecutors of Serbia and Montenegro is very good, said Vlado Susovic, state prosecutor of Montenegro. Susovic rejected the requests of newly elected federal prosecutor Vukasin Jokanovic, implying centralisation of prosecutor's office.
MONITOR

- If Djukanovic and parliamentary speaker Svetozar Marovic are aware that Montenegero and Serbia can prosper only in western economic and military integrations, then they should also be aware that the political party to which they belong (DPS) does not have a certain future which their career can rely on, the paper said in an editorial.

- Perfidious and forcible changes of federal constitution in 1989 caused the collapse of former Yugoslavia. Milosevic now tries to repeat the same story with the federal constitution which can also lead to the collapse of this entity called the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, former ethnic Albanian Kosovo leader Azem Vlasi said in an interview. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
